name: Photo Portals
description: Pass through an engraved photographic frame into a depth-aware image. Reverse to return, or bring a real Gaussian-splat scene.

compatibility: WebGL2 in current Chrome, Safari, Firefox, and Edge. Tested locally in Chromium and WebKit.
Mode A renders on demand. Low quality and a modest pixel ratio suit smaller devices. Reduced motion uses immediate manual positions.
Mode B uses Spark 2.3.1, Web Workers and WebAssembly. Its optional runtime loads only when opening a splat. Large scenes need substantial GPU memory.
Without WebGL2 or JavaScript, an illustrated static plate remains available.
Local JPEG/PNG/WebP files and grayscale depth maps stay in memory. Splat picker supports .ply, .splat, .ksplat, and .spz up to 64 MB.
notes: Mode A is a genuine projective depth mesh. Its vertices unfold into negative z while the camera passes the original picture plane. Returning uses the identical path and geometry.
The sample depth maps are artist estimates. They offer limited 2.5D parallax; they do not reconstruct hidden surfaces or create a complete navigable building. Some texture stretching is inherent.

Mode B is a clearly labeled loader, with no bundled reconstruction. No verified licensed splat corresponding to the sample photographs was available. Your real scene is decoded by Spark; a matching poster is captured from its registered viewpoint.
Scroll over the picture, drag upward on touch, use arrow keys, or scrub the slider. Outward scrolling at each end returns to page scrolling. Hold any intermediate position.
Photographs keep their Unsplash licenses. Local uploads and scene alignment stay in this session; settings and source exports never include private files.
reuse: Export the source and serve example.html over HTTP. Three.js, Spark, its embedded decoder/worker, licenses, and the photographs are bundled locally.
Import mount from index.js for the complete instrument, or createPortalViewer from viewer.js for a custom UI. transition.js is independent of rendering and sample content.
Pass {image, depth} as the fourth mount argument for your own photographic content. Depth is optional; without it, the image is flat and clearly labeled.
Call viewer.setSplat({url}) or {fileBytes, fileName} with an optional documented registration. Capture its poster after alignment, then use the same transition timeline.
